label: Edward Teller
narrative: Teller's presence in the room at Los Alamos on 16 February 1949 is the documented fact, and Los Alamos National Laboratory itself is the source for it. That places one of the two or three most access-privileged physicists in the United States - a man who within three years would co-found the Livermore laboratory and spend half a century inside the most tightly compartmented weapons programmes the country ran - in the earliest recorded scientific conference on anomalous aerial objects over American nuclear facilities. LANL records that the conference concluded the green fireballs were ultimately dismissed as a national security threat. That conclusion did not stop the Air Force from standing up Project Twinkle ten months later to instrument them. Teller was later associated with the Livermore laboratory throughout the era in which, according to whistleblower testimony collected by AAWSAP and by David Grusch, materials exploitation work was distributed across the DOE laboratory complex and its industrial partners. No document has been produced placing Teller inside such a programme. What the record does show is that when the United States first convened scientists to discuss unexplained objects over its nuclear archipelago, it convened them inside the contractor-operated laboratory system and not inside the Air Force's public UFO project.
